title: CladBench v1 Example
description: Universal schema for a single CladBench evaluation example. One JSON object per line in the JSONL datasets.

id.description: Stable identifier. Format: cb1-{NN}-{split}-{0001..} e.g. cb1-01-public-0042.

category.description: Category number 1-12 as defined in category_specs.md.

category_name.description: Human-readable category name for convenience. Must match category_specs.md.

format.description: Question format. Determines required fields in answer and grading.

split.description: Whether this example is in the public release set or the private holdout.

text.description: The full question prompt as it will be presented to the model.

options.description: Required for mcq and mcq_with_rationale. Choice labels (A, B, C...) are derived from index.

context.description: Optional structured context: time-series data, IFC snippet, building description. Presented before question.text.

candidates.description: Required for ranking. Items to be ranked. Labels are derived from index (a, b, c...).

answer.description: The reference answer in the format appropriate for this question.

choice.description: For mcq and mcq_with_rationale: the letter of the correct option.

text.description: For short_answer and open_answer: the reference answer text.

ranking.description: For ranking: ordered list of candidate labels (best first).

rationale.description: For mcq_with_rationale and some short_answer: the explanation/justification expected.

citation.description: Optional. Specific clause / standard / publication the answer cites. Used in regulation categories.

method.description: How to score a model's response against the answer. band_tolerance is used for judgement categories where +-1 band of the reference is acceptable.

rubric.description: Required for llm_judge_rubric. Scoring criteria for the LLM judge.

judge_model.description: Override the default LLM judge for this example. Defaults to Claude (latest).

case_sensitive.description: For exact_match: whether comparison is case-sensitive.

primary.description: Citable primary source (e.g. 'Approved Document L1A 2021, Table 4.1').

review_status.description: Curation review state. 'cross_validated' means other models agreed with the answer; 'reviewed' means Tamil read it; 'primary_source_verified' means the answer was checked against the primary document it cites. 'unverifiable' means the question was checked and the check could NOT settle it — the answer requires a source that is not obtainable, or modelling that has not been run. It is an outcome, not a gap, and such questions must not be counted as verified. The reason is carried in source.unverifiable_reason. 'primary_source_verified' is a stronger claim than 'cross_validated', because model agreement is not evidence — 14 of the answers replaced during cross-review were later found to be wrong.

verified_at.description: Date the answer was last checked against its primary source.

unverifiable_reason.description: Why the check could not settle this question, and what would settle it. Present only when review_status is 'unverifiable'.

correction.description: What verification changed, which determines what had to be redone. 'rewrite' — question or option text changed, so stored model responses were discarded and regenerated. 'rescore' — only the answer key changed, so stored responses were re-marked without re-running. 'citation' — provenance metadata only; nothing re-run, nothing re-scored.

curated_at.description: Date this record was last written by the curation tooling. It is a provenance timestamp, not a statement that a person reviewed the question. Verification against a primary source is recorded in verified_at; human sign-off is not currently recorded.

metadata.description: Free-form tags for slicing the dataset at evaluation time.

difficulty.description: Approximate difficulty for a domain expert.

policy_dependency.description: Whether the reference answer's correctness depends on a policy position that can move. 'live' means it rests on a regulation not yet in force, under open consultation, or commencing after the dataset as-at date; 'settled' means it does not. Assigned mechanically from the answer's content and never from how any model scored, so the split cannot be tuned to flatter a result. A 'live' answer is reproducible but not durable: the saved score always recomputes, while the ground truth expires.

policy_targets.description: Keys from cladbench.moving_targets this answer depends on, e.g. 'mees_nondom'. Absent or empty for settled questions.

as_at.description: For 'live' questions, the date the policy position in the reference answer was last established. Scores on this question are valid only as at this date.
